data.description:
## Context

Two consecutive successful macOS Gerrit Verify jobs after change 1730 still report tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py::test_benchmark_commit_count_is_ceil_per_pass at 21.05s and 29.38s. Closed ticket curricular-mean-cuckoo already removed the dominant redundant work and explicitly locks this contract at 3,000 tickets, 3,000 comments, 24 crash-safe import commits, and >=10x commit reduction. This follow-up must preserve that exact behavioral/performance-scale contract and remove only proven redundant work.

## Plan

1. Reproduce the exact N=3000 node on current origin/main with repeated wall-time samples and a full call-count/cumulative-time profile. Separate test construction, importer composition, validation, filesystem writes, Git index/commit subprocesses, materialization, and cleanup.
2. Form competing hypotheses from the profile and run one controlled experiment per hypothesis. Compare against the already-landed author-cache and stale-sweep optimization; do not infer from aggregate suite time.
3. Cross-check the ticket store for prior decisions and compare the proven mechanism with popular maintained OSS bulk-import/test patterns before proposing a change. The curricular-mean-cuckoo workload and durability constraints remain controlling.
4. If the remaining cost is redundant setup or production-path work, add a deterministic held-out oracle for the exact call/effect count, prove RED, implement the narrow optimization, and prove GREEN plus exact-defect mutation RED. If the remaining time is irreducible work needed for the locked scale contract, report that result and evaluate scheduling/tier placement without removing the test from macOS unless equivalent platform assurance is proven.
5. Verify the unchanged N=3000/6000-event/24-commit assertions, import idempotency, rollback, crash-resume, clean-index, author and stale-sweep lifecycle, focused unit/interface suites, lint, typecheck, and the full Gerrit Verify matrix. Report before/after macOS runner-seconds and overall critical-path effect.

## Test contract card

authoritative_contract: curricular-mean-cuckoo and tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py preserve N=3000, 6,000 events, exactly 24 crash-safe import commits, >=10x commit reduction, complete state, rollback, and resume.
trigger_preconditions: fresh real Git-backed store importing the fixed synthetic corpus through public rebar.import_tickets.
production_path: rebar.import_tickets through import composition, batch staging/commit, and materialization.
test_tier: real-Git integration on every supported CI platform currently executing this node.
observable_postcondition: identical ticket/comment state, event attribution, commit graph/count, clean index, and deterministic collaborator/effect counts with lower measured wall time.
negative_control: independent interactive writes, failure rollback, later-chunk resume, and existing-ticket imports retain current semantics.
collateral_invariants: no test, platform cell, mutation shard, coverage measurement, event validation, durability boundary, or contractual assertion is removed or weakened.
ci_gate: focused repeated benchmark evidence plus full Gerrit Verified gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Current macOS time over 20s is reproduced and individually attributed to concrete operations with call counts and cumulative time.
- [ ] The exact N=3000, 6,000-event, 24-commit, >=10x, complete-state, rollback, and crash-resume contracts remain unchanged and green.
- [ ] Any implementation is guarded by a held-out deterministic oracle, exact-defect mutation evidence, and negative controls for interactive/failure behavior.
- [ ] Ticket-store prior decisions and relevant maintained OSS practice are documented before remediation.
- [ ] Repeated same-host before/after results quantify test and runner-time savings; time remains evidence, not a flaky threshold.
- [ ] Focused suites, lint, typecheck, full Gerrit Verify, LLM-Review, and merge are green before closure.
data.title: Eliminate remaining macOS N=3000 import benchmark long pole
